title: Friday, November 27: Azuay votes Sunday; dry law starts at noon
notes:
Azuay heads to the polls on Sunday to elect a new mayor of Cuenca, a prefect and local councils, with electoral silence in force and the dry law starting at noon today. Plus Cuenca's new ban on two riders per motorcycle, the falling Mazar reservoir with the Colombia power link down, and a quieter election-weekend agenda.

In this episode:
Sunday's local elections: 272 polling places in Azuay, 7 am to 5 pm; dry law from Friday noon to Monday noon, $241 fines
Cuenca council bans two people riding one motorcycle; seven-day impound for violators
Mazar reservoir near its minimum as the power link with Colombia stays down after an attack
Constitutional Court clears a mining referendum in Santa Isabel
Clínica Santa Ana expansion; Cuenca to host the Copa Ecuador final on December 10
El Niño toll reaches 30; most coastal schools reopen
Bolivia and Peru revive their binational cabinet
Weekend in Cuenca: Deportivo Cuenca vs. Manta, Viernes Cusni market discounts, Drácula at Teatro Sucre, El Cuarentazo, ghost route at the Conceptas museum, Materia Architectures
Good to Know: where to vote, a rainy weekend, possible power cuts

title: Tuesday, November 24: Surprise blackouts as Mazar nears its limit
notes:
Unannounced power cuts hit Cuenca and several other cities on Monday night as the Mazar reservoir sat just over three meters above its critical level, and large industries are off the grid again until Thursday midnight. Plus the debate over a $500 minimum wage and what it means for retiree visas, El Niño floods in Galápagos and Guayaquil, a car bomb in Colombia, and a busy week of concerts, theater and marches in Cuenca.

Monday-night blackouts in Cuenca and across Ecuador; Mazar turbines switched off to save water
Large industries disconnected until Thursday midnight
Cuenca still has Ecuador's most expensive basic family basket

New building projects; international education congress; monigote sellers stay on Av. Primero de Mayo
Stadium legend Luis "Negro" Díaz dies at 90
Unions reject a proposed $500 minimum wage for 2027; retiree visa income requirement
El Niño floods in Galápagos and Guayaquil; Los Tiguerones leader returned from Spain
Car bomb in Villavicencio, Colombia; university march in Peru

title: Sunday, November 22: Mazar gets a brief reprieve

title: Tuesday, November 17: Mazar reservoir falls again
notes:
The Mazar reservoir behind the Paute hydro complex is dropping again and stopped generating this morning, while Cuenca's mayoral and prefect candidates debate this Friday ahead of the November 29 local elections. Plus early bonus and pension payments, Colombia's investment push, and a week of salsa, symphonic concerts and a bird expo in Cuenca.

In this episode:
Mazar reservoir drops toward its critical level; turbines stop generating
Debates for Cuenca mayor and Azuay prefect on Friday, November 20, at Teatro Pumapungo
Partial lane closure on the Cuenca–Azogues highway for the Gapal interchange
Noboa repeats plan for a new airport at Taura to serve Azuay and El Oro
El Niño red alert: heavy rain tonight in seven coastal and western provinces
Christmas bonus and IESS pensions paid early; CyberDay runs through Wednesday
Mining exports up a third in the first nine months
Colombia announces nearly 26 billion dollars in planned investment

title: Premiere: Welcome to The Cuenca Brief
notes:

When new episodes arrive (Cuenca time, UTC−5):
Sundays around 5:00 am: the week that was and the week ahead (up to 15 minutes)
Tuesdays around 4:00 pm: the latest news, for the trip home (up to 10 minutes)
